title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 6

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the exercise begin?
tasks.audioText: The aviation technology instructor has arranged a component identification exercise for Wednesday at ten. Students will work with training samples of fasteners, brackets and cable connectors. The sample table is in Laboratory 2. Each group should bring the illustrated glossary from the previous lesson and record unfamiliar terms for later discussion.
options: At ten on Wednesday
At nine on Wednesday
At ten on Thursday
At eleven on Wednesday

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which glossary should groups bring?
tasks.audioText: The aviation technology instructor has arranged a component identification exercise for Wednesday at ten. Students will work with training samples of fasteners, brackets and cable connectors. The sample table is in Laboratory 2. Each group should bring the illustrated glossary from the previous lesson and record unfamiliar terms for later discussion.
options: The maintenance glossary from the previous lesson
The illustrated glossary from the previous lesson
The component catalogue from the previous lesson
The safety checklist from the previous lesson

tasks.prompt: A trainee was asked to identify three components from a training aircraft diagram. She used the reference numbers to locate each item in the illustrated parts catalogue. The catalogue included a description and a drawing for each component. When two items looked similar, she checked the full part number rather than relying on appearance alone. Reading 1. What did the trainee use to locate each item?
options: The component colours in the photograph
The storage locations in the workshop
The reference numbers in the diagram
The supplier names in the parts list

tasks.prompt: How did she distinguish two similar components?
options: She compared the component colours
She measured the overall length
She compared the storage labels
She checked the full part number

tasks.prompt: The component ___ in the illustrated catalogue by its reference number.
options: can be identified
identify
is identifying yesterday
can identifying

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO details that help identify an aviation component accurately.
options: The colour of the storage shelf
The name of an unrelated passenger
Full part number
Reference number and catalogue description

tasks.prompt: A catalogue code that identifies one specific component is its part ___.
Two components look similar. What should you tell your colleague?
options: They look the same, so either one will do.
Let's compare the full part numbers before selecting a component.
Choose the first one you see.
The reference number is not important.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of aviation components in a logical order.
options: Compare the full part number and description
Read the reference number on the diagram
Record the identified component
Find the matching catalogue entry
correctOrder: Read the reference number on the diagram
Compare the full part number and description

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how a trainee can identify an unfamiliar component using a diagram and an illustrated parts catalogue.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response explains how to use a diagram and illustrated parts catalogue to identify an unfamiliar component (0–2); it includes checking references/item numbers and confirming the identification rather than relying on appearance alone (0–2); the explanation is clear with understandable grammar (0–2); component-identification/catalogue vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
